avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Potent CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 inducer; increases paroxetine metabolism and reduces efficacy; risk of serotonin syndrome
avoid_supplements.action: Discontinue St. John's Wort at least 2 weeks before starting paroxetine or avoid concurrent use

avoid_supplements.name: Tramadol
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Both inhibit serotonin reuptake and tramadol inhibits norepinephrine reuptake; significant serotonin syndrome risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; if essential, use lowest dose with close monitoring for serotonin syndrome symptoms

avoid_supplements.name: Linezolid
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Weak MAOI activity; combined serotonergic effect increases serotonin syndrome risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid use; if medically necessary, discontinue paroxetine 2 weeks prior and monitor closely

avoid_supplements.name: S-Adenosyl Methionine (SAM-e)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Serotonergic activity; may increase serotonin syndrome risk when combined with SSRIs
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use or use with caution under medical supervision

avoid_supplements.name: 5-Hydroxytryptophan (5-HTP)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Direct serotonin precursor; increases serotonergic activity and serotonin syndrome risk
avoid_supplements.action: Discontinue 5-HTP or avoid concurrent use with paroxetine

caution_supplements.name: Ginkgo biloba
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have mild antiplatelet effects; paroxetine increases bleeding risk through platelet dysfunction
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for signs of bleeding; consider periodic assessment if long-term concurrent use

caution_supplements.name: Omega-3 Fatty Acids (high-dose)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Modest antiplatelet and anticoagulant effects; additive with paroxetine's platelet effects
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for bleeding signs; moderate doses (≤2-3g EPA/DHA daily) generally safe

caution_supplements.name: Folic Acid and B-vitamins
caution_supplements.mechanism: May potentiate serotonergic effects; generally supportive for mood
caution_supplements.action: Safe to use; monitor mood and anxiety symptoms with concurrent use

avoid_foods.name: Tyramine-rich foods (if any MAOI interaction occurs)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Paroxetine has minimal MAOI activity, but tyramines could theoretically elevate blood pressure if combined with unintended serotonergic potentiation
avoid_foods.action: No strict tyramine avoidance required with paroxetine monotherapy, but counsel to limit aged cheeses, cured meats if switching from MAOIs

caution_foods.name: Grapefruit and grapefruit juice
caution_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibitor; may moderately increase paroxetine levels, though paroxetine is primarily metabolized by CYP2D6
caution_foods.action: Moderate consumption acceptable; excessive intake (>1L daily) should be avoided

caution_foods.name: Caffeinated beverages (coffee, tea, energy drinks)
caution_foods.mechanism: Caffeine potentiates CNS stimulation and may increase anxiety, tremor, or insomnia in susceptible individuals
caution_foods.action: Limit caffeine intake; counsel patients to monitor for increased anxiety or sleep disturbance

caution_foods.name: Alcohol
caution_foods.mechanism: CNS depressant; may potentiate sedation, impair judgment, and worsen depression; increases bleeding risk
caution_foods.action: Advise minimal or no alcohol consumption; counsel on impaired cognition and fall risk

monitoring_notes: Monitor for serotonin syndrome symptoms (agitation, confusion, rapid heart rate, muscle rigidity) especially with supplements or drugs affecting serotonin. Assess bleeding risk and symptoms (bruising, petechiae) as paroxetine inhibits platelet aggregation; caution with anticoagulants or antiplatelet agents.
